nodes.title: CONTENTS
nodes.summary: The provided text outlines the contents of a basketball school curriculum, detailing ten modules. Each module includes a 'Tip-Off', 'Warm-Up' activities, 'Game Time' drills, and concludes with 'Buzzer Beater' and 'Final Buzzer' sections. Specific drills within each module cover various player combinations (1-on-1, 2-on-1, 3-on-2, etc.), game scenarios, shooting, passing, dribbling, and defensive strategies. Some modules also feature 'Competition Ladder' or 'Off-Court' activities.

nodes.title: TIP-OFF
nodes.summary: The text describes 'TIP-OFF', a 5-minute opening huddle for coaches to welcome players and set daily expectations. It outlines five key components: CALL IN (gathering players), CONNECTIONS (physical greetings), COMMUNICATIONS (sharing information), COMMENCEMENT (preparing for camp), and CHEER (an enthusiastic group cheer). Additionally, it mentions MODULE 1: FULL OUTLINE, which includes WARM-UP and Basketball School.

nodes.title: WARM-UP
nodes.summary: The provided text outlines the 'Warm-up' module of a basketball program, detailing two activities: 'Partner Tag Game' and '4-on-2 Passing Rondo'. The 'Partner Tag Game' focuses on agility, creativity, and changing speed through various tagging scenarios. The '4-on-2 Passing Rondo' emphasizes ball possession, passing accuracy, and defensive pressure within a defined space. Both activities include specific instructions on setup, gameplay, scoring (optional for rondo), key concepts, staff roles, and guiding questions to enhance player development. The text concludes by indicating that 'Game Time' follows the warm-up.

nodes.title: GAME TIME
nodes.summary: This text outlines Module 1 of the Basketball School's 'Game Time' section, which focuses on player development through activities designed to mimic basketball. Each activity is presented with a standardized format including name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions, encouraging coaches to adapt them. Several specific 'Game Time' activities are listed.

nodes.title: Game Time Activities: Skill Development Through Simulated Play
nodes.summary: The 'GAME TIME' section of the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum focuses on developing players' technical and tactical skills through simulated game scenarios. Each activity is meticulously structured with details on name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, load variations, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions, encouraging coaches to adapt and expand. The curriculum outlines specific activities like '1-ON-1 BLIND' and '2-ON-2 CHANGING LOCATIONS', detailing their objectives, gameplay mechanics, scoring systems, and various 'load' modifications to challenge players. '1-ON-1 BLIND' emphasizes creating advantage and varied finishes, while '2-ON-2 CHANGING LOCATIONS' focuses on maintaining advantage, attacking help defense, and defensive stops, with specific rules and 'lava' concepts introduced for younger players.

nodes.title: Basketball Drills: 2-on-2, 1-on-1, and 3-on-3 Continuous Play
nodes.summary: This section of the Basketball School curriculum under GAME TIME covers three drills: 2-on-2 Changing Locations, 1-on-1 Create Space, and 3-on-3 Half-Court Continuous. The 2-on-2 drill focuses on offensive and defensive positioning. The 1-on-1 drill emphasizes creating space and shooting off the dribble within a limited time and dribble count, with specific rules for defense and scoring. The 3-on-3 drill is a continuous half-court game where teams rotate after scores, focusing on beating initial and help defense and identifying open players, with variations for younger players and specific 'lava' rules to enforce spacing and movement.

nodes.title: 2-on-1 and 3-on-2 Drills for Offensive Advantage
nodes.summary: This section details two basketball drills within the 'GAME TIME' module of a Basketball School curriculum. The '2-ON-1 I MORE' drill focuses on offensive players making quick decisions and scoring within two passes against a single defender, emphasizing ROB shots (Range, Open, Balance). It includes variations for different age groups and scoring for both offense and defense. The '3-ON-2 CONVERT THE ADVANTAGE' drill involves a 3-on-2 offensive scenario aiming for quick scores within 10-second 'bursts', also highlighting ROB shots and decision-making. This drill features 'lava' rules for younger players, advanced load examples, and scoring that determines a winning team. Both drills aim to develop offensive efficiency and defensive disruption, with guiding questions to reinforce key concepts.

nodes.title: Game Time Drills and Off-Court Learning
nodes.summary: This section outlines various basketball drills and activities within the 'GAME TIME' module, including '3-on-2 Convert the Advantage' and a detailed '5-on-5 Loads-Based' game with specific rules, scoring, key concepts, guiding questions, and variations for younger players. It also introduces 'OFF-COURT' activities designed for further learning through video analysis and other exercises, covering topics like defense, shot selection, and ball handling. Finally, the 'BUZZER BEATER' component is described as a daily reflection activity using a player notebook to assess performance and learning.

nodes.title: FINAL BUZZER
nodes.summary: The Final Buzzer is a brief, 5-minute closing huddle where coaches see players off. It includes five key components: verbally calling players in, offering physical connections, delivering important communications, concluding with a debrief on learnings, and ending with an enthusiastic group cheer.

nodes.title: Camp Opening and Warm-Up Activities
nodes.summary: This section outlines the initial components of a basketball camp module. It details the 'Tip-Off,' a brief opening huddle for setting expectations, comprising five key elements: Call In, Connections, Communications, Commencement, and Cheer. Following this, it presents the 'Competition Ladder,' offering various competitive formats like 1v1, 2v2, 3v3, and shooting contests, which can be structured with different loads. The 'Warm-Up' section is then introduced, focusing on preparing players physically and mentally through activities like 'Small Space Dribble Knockout' and 'Pass Keepaway.' The 'Small Space Dribble Knockout' is described in detail, including its objective, playing space, equipment, description, examples of loads, scoring, key concepts, staff roles, and guiding questions, all aimed at developing ball manipulation and defensive skills.

nodes.title: Warm-up Drills and Game Time Introduction
nodes.summary: This section outlines two warm-up drills, 'Small Space Dribble Knockout' and 'Pass Keepaway,' both 10 minutes long, focusing on ball handling, stealing, passing under pressure, and spatial awareness. It then introduces the 'Game Time' section, explaining its purpose of developing players through game-like activities and detailing the format for each activity. Finally, it describes the '1-on-1 Rooted' drill, a 16-minute Game Time activity designed to improve finishing and defensive contesting skills, with specific rules, scoring, and variations.

nodes.title: Game Time Drills: 1-on-1 and 3-on-3 Continuous Play
nodes.summary: This section of the curriculum outlines two basketball drills under the 'GAME TIME' module: 'I-ON-1 ROOTED' and 'I-ON-I ADVANCE THE BALL', and '3-ON-3 HALF-COURT CONTINUOUS'. The 'I-ON-1 ROOTED' drill is briefly introduced with a visual of a potential starting position. The 'I-ON-I ADVANCE THE BALL' drill, lasting 16 minutes, focuses on players advancing the ball against pressure within a 10-second time limit, using available space and one ball per basket. It details scoring for both offense and defense, emphasizes concepts like containing the ball, and provides various 'loads' or modifications such as defenders holding a ball or adding a trailing defender. Staff roles include timekeeping and score communication. The '3-ON-3 HALF-COURT CONTINUOUS' drill, lasting 20 minutes, involves teams of three playing half-court with continuous rotation after scores or defensive stops. It utilizes all available baskets and one ball per basket. Scoring is based on made baskets and defensive stops. Key concepts include beating initial defense and identifying open players. The drill offers 'loads' that restrict offensive players from receiving the ball in certain 'lava' areas (paint or inside the 3PT line) and emphasizes spacing. Staff roles involve scorekeeping and ensuring varied starting angles. Visuals are provided for both drills.

nodes.title: Basketball Drills: 3v3, 1v1, 4v4, and 5v5 Variations
nodes.summary: This section outlines four basketball drills within the 'Game Time' module: 3-on-3 Half-Court Continuous, 1-on-1 Blind Shooting, 4-on-4 Defensive Shutdown, and 5-on-5 Loads-Based. Each drill includes details on playing space, equipment, a description of how to play, scoring methods, key concepts to focus on, examples of variations or 'loads' to adjust difficulty, and the role of the staff. The 1-on-1 drill emphasizes quick shooting and offensive advantage creation. The 4-on-4 drill focuses on defensive intensity and ball pressure. The 5-on-5 drill centers on spacing and efficient shot hunting, with various 'lava' rules and scoring adjustments for different skill levels.

nodes.title: Game Play, Reflection, and Closing Activities
nodes.summary: This text outlines a 20-minute '5-on-5 Loads-Based' basketball game activity. It details team formation, scoring (1 point per 3 baskets), key concepts like spacing and shot efficiency, and provides guiding questions for players. Various 'loads' or rule variations are explained, including 'lava' zones, escape rules, and penalties for turnovers or lack of ball pressure. The staff's role in organizing and teaching is also specified. Following the game, the 'Buzzer Beater' component involves player reflection using notebooks on their performance and learning. The 'Final Buzzer' is a brief closing huddle with five parts: Call In, Connections, Communications, Conclusion, and a Cheer.

nodes.title: Camp Opening and Warm-Up Activities
nodes.summary: This section outlines the initial stages of a basketball camp curriculum, starting with the 'Tip-Off' which is a brief opening huddle (under 5 minutes) designed to welcome players, set expectations, and build team spirit through specific components like 'Call In', 'Connections', 'Communications', 'Commencement', and 'Cheer'. Following the 'Tip-Off', the 'Warm-Up' section details activities to prepare players physically and mentally. Two specific warm-up games are described: 'Tail Tag', a 10-minute agility and ball manipulation game where players try to steal each other's bibs, and 'Team Tag', another 10-minute game focused on agility, teamwork, and ball manipulation, involving 'escapers' and 'taggers' competing against time. Both games include variations ('Examples of Loads'), staff roles, and guiding questions to enhance the experience.

nodes.title: Warm-up and Game Time Drills
nodes.summary: This section outlines warm-up and game time activities for a basketball camp. The warm-up includes 'Team Tag,' a 10-minute agility and team competition drill focusing on speed and support. The 'Game Time' section introduces various drills designed to develop technical and tactical basketball skills through gameplay. Specific drills detailed include '2-on-2 Around the Cone' (10 minutes) focusing on offensive decision-making and defensive recovery, and '1-on-2 Conversion into 2-on-1 Back' (12 minutes) emphasizing pressure handling and disruptive defense. Each drill is presented with its duration, playing space, equipment, description, scoring, examples of variations ('loads'), staff roles, and guiding questions.

nodes.title: Game Time Drills: Conversion, Separation, and Scramble
nodes.summary: This section outlines three basketball drills for a school camp curriculum: '1-on-2 Conversion into 2-on-1 Back' (12 min), '1-on-1+1 Create Separation' (16 min), and '3-on-3 Scramble' (10 min). Each drill details playing space, equipment, description, scoring, key concepts, examples of loads (variations), guiding questions, and staff roles. The drills focus on developing offensive and defensive skills such as handling pressure, disruptive defense, creating advantages, scrambling, and recovering. They are designed to be played on half-courts with specific player roles and transition mechanics, with scoring systems and load variations to adapt difficulty and focus.

nodes.title: 3-on-3 Game Scenarios: Scramble and Three Trips
nodes.summary: This section details two basketball drills for a school camp curriculum: '3-on-3 Scramble' and '3-on-3 Three Trips'. The '3-on-3 Scramble' is a 10-minute drill focused on defensive scrambling and recovery, with variations for difficulty and pace. The '3-on-3 Three Trips' is an 18-minute drill emphasizing offensive and defensive transitions and spacing, also with modifications for different age groups and skill levels.

nodes.title: Game Time Drills and Off-Court Learning
nodes.summary: This section details three basketball drills within the 'Game Time' module: '3-on-3 Three Trips' (visual sequence provided), 'Shooting Ladder' (focusing on jump shots from different ranges with specific scoring and load examples), and '5-on-5 Loads-Based' (a team game with point scoring and various load examples to teach spacing, defense, and offensive efficiency). It also introduces 'Off-Court' activities designed to enhance learning through methods like video analysis, vocabulary exercises, and diagram design, covering key basketball concepts.

nodes.title: Off-Court Learning, Reflection, and Closing Activities
nodes.summary: This section outlines the 'OFF-COURT' component of the Basketball School curriculum, which expands on 'Game Time' learning through activities like video analysis, vocabulary, and diagram design, covering topics such as Space and Advantage, Disruptive Defense, Shot Selection, Ball Movement, Creative Finishes, and Ball Manipulation. It also details the 'BUZZER BEATER' reflection session where players use their notebooks to answer questions about their performance and learning. Finally, it describes the 'FINAL BUZZER,' a brief closing huddle that includes calling players in, establishing connections, communicating information, concluding the module, and ending with a group cheer.

nodes.title: Camp Opening, Competition Formats, and Warm-Up Drills
nodes.summary: This text outlines the initial segments of a basketball camp curriculum. It details the 'Tip-Off,' a brief opening huddle for welcoming players and setting expectations, comprising five key components: Call In, Connections, Communications, Commencement, and Cheer. Following this, the 'Competition Ladder' section presents various competitive formats (1v1, 2v2, 3v3, shooting contests) that can be integrated into the camp's 'Game Time' to provide structure and encourage player problem-solving. The 'Warm-Up' section is then introduced, focusing on activities to prepare players physically and mentally. A specific warm-up drill, the '1-on-1 Elbow Race,' is described in detail, including its objective (creative finishing, ball manipulation), setup, execution, scoring, staff roles, and guiding questions, with examples of 'loads' to modify the drill's difficulty.

nodes.title: Warm-up Drills and Game Time Introduction
nodes.summary: This text chunk details two warm-up drills for a basketball camp: the 'I-ON-1 ELBOW RACE' and the 'I-ON-I SLALOM'. Both drills are 10 minutes long and focus on creative finishing and ball manipulation skills, with variations in equipment, playing space, and specific load examples. The 'I-ON-1 ELBOW RACE' involves a race to score a lay-up after crossover dribbles, while the 'I-ON-I SLALOM' incorporates cones and a defender for a slalom dribbling challenge. The text also introduces the 'GAME TIME' section of the curriculum, explaining its purpose of developing players through game-like activities and outlining the format for these activities. It concludes by listing several 'Variable Shooting' drills that fall under the 'GAME TIME' category.

nodes.title: Game Time Activities and Drills
nodes.summary: The 'Game Time' section of the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum outlines various basketball activities and games designed for player development. Each activity is presented with a detailed format including name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, load examples, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. Specific activities covered are Variable Shooting, 2-on-2 Line Start to Post-Ups, and 1-on-1 Guided Post-Ups, each with unique objectives, rules, and developmental focuses such as adaptive shooting, post-up play, and defensive strategies.

nodes.title: Post-Up and 3-on-2 Shooting Drills
nodes.summary: This section details two basketball drills: 'I-ON-I GUIDED POST-UPS' and '3-ON-2 SHOOTING'. The post-up drill involves offensive players working in pairs near the block, with defenders influencing their move towards the basket and contesting shots after one dribble. Modifications for younger players and higher numbers are included, along with staff roles, key concepts like decision-making and defensive techniques, and guiding questions. The 3-on-2 shooting drill focuses on offensive spacing and creating scoring opportunities within a half-court setting, with a limit on dribbles and a focus on attacking closeouts. It also outlines player positioning, defensive strategies, scoring, staff responsibilities, and key concepts related to spacing and defense.

nodes.title: Game Time Drills and Off-Court Learning
nodes.summary: This section details several basketball drills and off-court activities. The 'Game Time' section includes '3-on-2 Shooting' with specific rules, '4-on-4 Half-Court Continuous with a Random Start' focusing on offensive and defensive strategies within a 14-second shot clock, and '5-on-5 Loads-Based' where teams earn points by scoring three baskets. Both 4-on-4 and 5-on-5 drills outline playing space, equipment, descriptions, scoring, examples of loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. The 'Off-Court' section describes activities designed to enhance learning from 'Game Time' sessions, including video analysis and various exercises related to key basketball concepts like spacing, defense, shot selection, and ball handling.

nodes.title: Off-Court Learning, Reflection, and Closing
nodes.summary: This section outlines the components of the Basketball School curriculum beyond on-court play. The OFF-COURT section focuses on reinforcing Game Time learning through activities like video analysis, vocabulary, and design tasks, covering topics such as space, defense, shot selection, ball movement, finishes, and manipulation. The BUZZER BEATER segment is a daily reflection period where players use their notebooks to answer questions about their performance, learning, and areas for improvement. Finally, the FINAL BUZZER is a brief closing huddle that includes calling players in, offering connections, communicating important information, concluding the module's learnings, and ending with a group cheer.

nodes.title: Off-Court Learning, Reflection, and Closing Activities
nodes.summary: This section outlines the 'OFF-COURT' components of the Basketball School curriculum. The 'OFF-COURT' section expands on 'Game Time' learning through activities like video analysis, vocabulary exercises, and diagram design, covering topics such as Space and Advantage, Defense, Shot Selection, Ball Movement, Finishing, and Ball Manipulation. The 'BUZZER BEATER' is a daily reflection activity where players use their notebooks to answer questions about their performance and learning. The 'FINAL BUZZER' is a brief closing huddle that includes calling players in, offering connections, communicating important information, debriefing on learnings, and ending with a group cheer.

structure.title: MODULE 8: FULL OUTLINE

This opening huddle, lasting under 5 minutes, involves players being called in, receiving connections and communications (news, rules, expectations), being primed for the camp's start (Commencement), and ending with an enthusiastic cheer. The module also briefly mentions a 'Competition Ladder'.

nodes.title: Warm-Up and Game Time Activities
nodes.summary: This section outlines the WARM-UP phase of the basketball camp curriculum, which includes activities to prepare players physically and mentally. Two specific warm-up games are detailed: PASS TOUCHDOWN, a non-dribbling passing game focused on scoring in an endzone, and OBSTACLE COURSE TAG, a tag game that can incorporate obstacles and dribbling. The section then transitions to GAME TIME, explaining that these activities are designed to mimic basketball and foster player development. Each GAME TIME activity follows a structured format and a list of these activities is provided, including various shooting and game-play scenarios.

nodes.title: Game Time Drills and Activities
nodes.summary: The 'Game Time' module focuses on developing players through simulated game scenarios and activities designed to mimic basketball. Each activity is presented with a consistent format including description, scoring, and coaching guidance. Specific drills detailed are '1-ON-1 BIG ADVANTAGE SHOOTING,' which emphasizes quick shooting and defensive closeouts, and '3-ON-2 INTO 2-ON-2 HALF-COURT,' a transition drill that combines offensive advantage play with continuous action. Both drills include specific rules, scoring, key concepts, load variations, staff roles, and guiding questions to enhance player learning.

nodes.title: Game Time Drills: Transition, Ball Advancement, and Drive & Kick
nodes.summary: This section details three basketball drills: '3-on-2 into 2-on-2 Half-Court' which focuses on transition play; '2-on-2 Advance the Ball' emphasizing offensive ball progression with restricted passing and disruptive defense; and '1-on-1+1 Drive and Kick' which combines driving, passing, and re-spacing to create scoring opportunities. Each drill includes descriptions of playing space, equipment, rules, scoring, key concepts, variations (loads), staff roles, and guiding questions for players.

nodes.title: Drive and Kick and Continuous 3-on-3 Drills
nodes.summary: This section details two basketball drills: 'I-ON-I+I DRIVE AND KICK' and '3-ON-3 HALF-COURT CONTINUOUS'. The 'Drive and Kick' drill focuses on offensive players driving, passing to a teammate, and then re-spacing to get open for a 1-on-1 opportunity, emphasizing space creation and creative finishing. The '3-on-3 Half-Court Continuous' drill involves rapid transitions between offensive and defensive teams in a half-court setting, focusing on beating defense and identifying open players. Both drills include variations for younger players, scoring rules, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions.

nodes.title: Game Time: 5-on-5 Loads-Based and Closing Activities
nodes.summary: This section details 'Game Time' activities within Module 8 of the NBA Basketball School curriculum. It outlines two game formats: '3-on-3 Half-Court Continuous' (briefly mentioned) and a more detailed '5-on-5 Loads-Based' game. The 5-on-5 game is a 24-minute activity using available baskets, with teams of 5 playing to 3 baskets for 1 point, and continuous rotation of teams. Specific 'loads' or gameplay restrictions are provided, varying by age group, focusing on shot efficiency, ball pressure, and floor spacing, with examples like designated 'lava' zones and scoring limitations. Staff roles involve organization, substitution, and teaching. The module also includes a 'Buzzer Beater' reflective activity using player notebooks and a 'Final Buzzer' closing huddle with specific components: Call In, Connections, Communications, Conclusion, and Cheer.

nodes.title: FINAL BUZZER
nodes.summary: The text describes the 'Final Buzzer,' a 5-minute closing huddle for basketball school, comprising five key parts: Call In, Connections, Communications, Conclusion, and Cheer. It also briefly mentions Module 9: Full Outline for Basketball School, including 'Tip-Off' as a component.

nodes.title: TIP-OFF
nodes.summary: The text describes 'TIP-OFF', a 5-minute opening huddle for coaches to set daily expectations for players. It outlines five key components: CALL IN (gathering players), CONNECTIONS (physical greetings), COMMUNICATIONS (sharing information), COMMENCEMENT (preparing for camp), and CHEER (an enthusiastic group cheer). Additionally, it mentions that MODULE 9 of Basketball School covers the WARM-UP section.

nodes.title: WARM-UP
nodes.summary: This text details warm-up activities for basketball, specifically 'Steal the Cone' and 'Steal the Tail Gate Tag'. 'Steal the Cone' is a game for groups of three focused on deceptive movements, where perimeter players try to tag a cone defended by one player within a limited area and time. 'Steal the Tail Gate Tag' is a game for larger groups emphasizing agility and teamwork, where offensive players with bibs navigate through cone gates while evading defenders. Both activities include descriptions of playing space, equipment, rules, variations, staff roles, scoring (for 'Steal the Tail Gate Tag'), key concepts, and guiding questions. The text also references accompanying images and concludes by transitioning to 'GAME TIME'.

nodes.title: Game Time Drills: 3-on-3, 2-on-1, and 4-on-4 Variations
nodes.summary: This section details four basketball drills under the 'GAME TIME' module: '3-on-3 Around the Cone,' '2-on-1 I More,' '3-on-3 Random Possession Change,' and '4-on-4 Changing Rims.' nodes.title: WARM-UP
nodes.summary: This text outlines warm-up procedures for a basketball program, specifically detailing two drills: Functional Movement Exploration and 1-on-1 Block Races. Functional Movement Exploration encourages players to creatively repeat movements in diverse ways, with examples like varied lunges and squats, and staff guidance to avoid identical repetitions. 1-on-1 Block Races involve a competitive lay-up drill with variations such as weak-hand scoring and ball manipulation, aiming to develop creative finishing and ball skills, with a scoring system of first to four points. The text also indicates a subsequent 'GAME TIME' section.

nodes.title: Game Time Activities and Structure
nodes.summary: The 'Game Time' section of the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum focuses on developing players through simulated game scenarios. Each activity is meticulously structured with details on time, space, equipment, description, scoring, load variations, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions, encouraging coaches to adapt and expand. Specific activities detailed include '2-ON-1+1 CLOSEOUTS' (emphasizing ROB shots and advantage maintenance), '3-ON-3 CHANGING LOCATIONS' (focusing on advantage creation, help defense, and ball stopping with 'lava' rules), and '2-ON-3+1 CONTINUOUS' (highlighting space creation, advantage maintenance, and disruptive defense with a supporting '+1' player). Load examples and guiding questions are provided for each to tailor the drills for different skill levels and encourage strategic thinking.

Each drill outlines the number of players, duration, playing space, equipment, description of play, scoring, key concepts, examples of loads (including variations for younger players), staff roles, and guiding questions. The drills focus on offensive and defensive strategies, spacing, transition play, and decision-making in various game-like scenarios.

nodes.title: Game Time Activities and Reflection

Both 3-on-3 and 4-on-4 activities include adaptable rules ('loads') for different age groups and skill levels, with staff roles and guiding questions provided for each.
